lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1677: the log leaves in an envelope

Item four of "fix all existing issues one through six": #82, Sentry's
@password:filter still taking a block from roughly a third of the log sends
after OTA-1520.

RE-MEASURED FIRST
711 delivered events from 09-03/04 in the inbox: 209 of them (29%) still lost a
block, 273 blocks, 93,210 characters. OTA-1520 worked exactly as far as it
claimed — the loss went from whole 15,000-character parts to ~400-character
blocks — but the scrubber was still being handed English, and the surviving
neighbours finally named what it takes: 219 of the 273 holes sit in SALVAGE
prose, and one of the four rotating curio lines in salvagePools.ts reads
"Nobody authored this piece" — `auth` inside "authored", the no-word-boundary
match 1520 predicted and could not yet see. The other 54 are two blocks that
recur across re-sent bundles: a haul naming a "…of Secrets" armour, and an
NPC's line. Sentry's Safe Fields could not exempt it (the relay already prints
that finding: the rule runs on chunkBlocks.0, .1, …), and a fantasy log cannot
avoid "secret" or "authored".

SO THE TEXT STOPS BEING TEXT IN TRANSIT
Each block is base64 on the device — UTF-8 then base64, by hand, because the
runtime guarantees neither TextEncoder nor btoa — and decoded by the relay when
the event says `chunkEncoding: base64`. The base64 alphabet has no `@`, no `.`,
no space and no word: @password, @email, @ip and @creditcard have nothing to
match, whatever the prose says and whatever a future default rule says. This is
the class fix — a content-scrubbing redactor is never handed content — where
rewording one curio line would have been the next whack-a-mole (the three
"…of Secrets" armours were next in line, and renaming items is a save
migration).

`chunkChars` stays the RAW receipt, so the relay's shortfall check is
unchanged. A block Sentry replaced anyway is not valid base64 and stands in the
reassembly as the literal "[Filtered]", exactly as visible as before. Pre-1677
events carry no `chunkEncoding` and reassemble as plain text, as they always
did — the branch is opt-in.

PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED: the suite runs Sentry's own pattern over a real 400 KB
delivered log from the inbox, block by block — the text trips it, no envelope
does — and checks the hand encoder against Node's base64 on every one of those
blocks, plus the four curio lines and the three armour names by name.

The task's second finding (release/dist null on every event) was closed by
OTA-1592 / task #109.

- app/diagnostics/sentryTransport.ts — encodeLogBlock, LOG_BLOCK_ENCODING;
  the inline sender encodes every block and names the encoding.
- .github/workflows/sentry-inbox.yml — decode_block; the base64 branch before
  the join and the receipt check.
- __tests__/ota1677TheLogLeavesInAnEnvelope.test.ts — 9 tests.
- __tests__/ota1520 / ota1518 / ota1505 — the extra-shape pins repointed to
  the encoded array (1505 decodes before it compares).
